In connection with the attached file on the above
subject, Mr. Yue Ding Ih, Ranking Political Agent in Shanghai,
came to this office on December 14, 1934, and informed the
undersigned that the four communist suspects named Wong Kiu Zeh
Ts (黄九子) et al arrested on December 8, 1934, in the Kashing
Road District are informers in the employ of the Special Branch
of the local Public Safety Bureau. These individuals, in
order to cloak their activities, are known to the Chinese
Authorities to be in touch with certain communist elements
from whom they obtain from time to time quantities of communist
literature ostensibly for the purpose of distribution. It
is the policy of the local Chinese Authorities, in view of
any forthcoming Red anniversary, to secure as much communist
literature as possible either for intelligence purposes or
for destruction in order to prevent it from being disseminated.
In conclusion, Mr. Yue expresses the desire
that the Municipal Police in this particular case will raise
no objection at the next hearing on December 17 when an
application for the extradition of the aforementioned suspects
will be made by the Chinese Authorities.

第一被告 黄九子

不利证据                                      有利证据

1934年12月8日被捕时，第一被告正将一包物品交给第二被告高德山，经检查发现其中含有约1,200份不同种类的共产党传单，内容涉及“北方抗日”、“纪念十二月一日广州起义”、“反对国民党第五次剿共运动”以及11月20日出版的《青年真理报》第72期，该期报道了中国红军最近的胜利以及工部局对人力车夫的压迫。据第一被告称，这些宣传品是第三被告钱成于12月7日晚放入其房间的。第一被告的父亲看到包裹内容的性质后，让儿子将其移除。儿子去寻找钱成但未找到，因此请求与钱成相识的第二被告将这些宣传品移除并交还给钱成。正是在移交包裹时，两人被捕。第一被告至今未能说明钱成为何要将此类宣传品放入其房间，也未向警方提供此类事情持续了多久的任何线索。另外值得注意的是，在搜查黄九子的房间时，在其中发现了少量共产党宣传品。      没有证据表明第一被告曾参与亲共活动，也没有证据证明他在被捕时是共产党员。仅凭在其房间内发现的几本书籍不足以证实他是活跃分子的指控。

pages.en:
-2-

2nd Accused KOH TUH SAI

Evidence Against

At the time the 2nd accused was arrested he was actually in possession of a bundle containing a large number of communistic pamphlets which had a few seconds before been handed over to him by Wong Kiu Zeh Ts, 1st accused. He has admitted to the police and the Court that the literature found in his possession was given to him by the 1st accused who informed him that it had been brought to his house by the 3rd accused Chien Zung. Further the 2nd accused stated that it was his intention to return the literature to Chien Zung but he has offered no reason why the literature should be given back to Chien Zung, if that person, as is claimed, is an agent of the man named Han Lu Hao, an employee of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau. The piece of paper found in the possession of Koh Tuh Sai bearing the name and telephone number of Han Lu Hao at the Public Safety Bureau was not written by that individual but most probably by the 2nd accused from information supplied to him by the 3rd or 4th accused.

Evidence For

There is no evidence that the 2nd accused has been concerned in the propagation of communism. There is ample evidence from the 1st and 3rd accused to show that it was not the intention of the 2nd accused either to keep the literature found in his possession nor was it his intention to distribute it. The paper found in his possession shows to a certain extent that he was in contact with an agent of the Shanghai Public Safety Bureau named Han Lu Hao and apparently that he was being employed in the detection of communists. Although a search was made of the home of the 2nd accused there was nothing of an incriminating nature found.

3rd Accused CHIEN ZUNG alias LING MING SUNG

Evidence Against

The 3rd accused has admitted having taken the literature to the home of the 1st accused but states that he did not give instructions that it should be handed over the 2nd accused. He claimed that the literature was handed to him by the 4th accused Wong Ah Sa alias Ting Hoong Chuen with instructions to place it in the home of the 1st accused, but that he did not know for what purpose the literature was intended.

Evidence For

The accused openly admitted that he took the literature to the home of the 1st accused and led Police to the home of the 4th accused from whom he obtained the literature and where a certain quantity of communist literature was seized. Further the accused has stated that he is employed as a secret agent or "second" by Han Lu Hao of the Public Safety Bureau which declaration has been substantiated by information obtained from the Public Safety Bureau.

第二被告 高德山

不利证据

第二被告被捕时，实际上持有一包大量共产主义小册子，这些册子是几秒钟前由第一被告黄九子交给他的。他已向警方和法庭承认，在他身上发现的宣传品是由第一被告给他的，第一被告告知他这些宣传品是第三被告钱成带到他家的。此外，第二被告声称他打算将宣传品归还给钱成，但他没有提出理由说明如果此人如所称是上海公安局雇员韩鲁浩（Han Lu Hao）的代理人，为何要将宣传品归还给钱成。在高德山身上发现的一张写有公安局韩鲁浩姓名和电话号码的纸条并非由该人书写，而很可能是第二被告根据第三或第四被告提供的信息写下的。

有利证据

没有证据表明第二被告参与了共产主义的传播。来自第一和第三被告的大量证据表明，第二被告既无意保留在他身上的宣传品，也无意分发它们。在他身上发现的纸条在某种程度上表明他与上海公安局名为韩鲁浩的代理人有联系，并且显然受雇于侦缉共产党分子。虽然对第二被告的家进行了搜查，但未发现任何具有定罪性质的物品。

第三被告 钱成，化名林明生

不利证据

第三被告承认曾将宣传品带到第一被告家中，但声称他没有指示将其交给第二被告。他声称宣传品是由第四被告王阿四（化名丁洪春）交给他的，并指示将其放在第一被告家中，但他不知道这些宣传品的用途是什么。

有利证据

被告公开承认他将宣传品带到了第一被告家中，并带领警察前往第四被告家中，他从那里获得了宣传品，并在该处查获了一定数量的共产党宣传品。此外，被告声明他受雇于公安局的韩鲁浩，担任秘密代理人或“线人”，这一声明已得到从公安局获得的信息证实。

4th Accused WONG AH SZ alias TING HOONG CHUEN

Evidence Against
Chien Zung 3rd accused when arrested by Police at 9 p.m.
8.12.34 was questioned with regard to the literature found
in the possession of the 1st and 2nd accused at the time of
their arrest. He stated that he had obtained the literature
from one Wong Ah Sz alias Ting Hoong Chuen who resided at
No. 235 Urga Road. The police raided this address and
there arrested the 4th accused as named. A search of the
room occupied by the man revealed a quantity of communist
literature similar in nature to that seized from the 1st
and 2nd accused. Wong Ah Sz was closely questioned and
claimed that he obtained the literature found in his house
and that handed over to Chien Zung on 7.12.34 for disposal
in Wong Kiu Zeh Ts' house from a Cantonese, a member of the
Communist Party. He admitted under interrogation that the
Cantonese often visits him at his home but that he has
nothing to do with his (Wong's) political activity. He
admitted having been a member of the Communist Party until
January 1934, when he surrendered to the local Bureau of
Public Safety. There is very little doubt that Wong Ah
Sz 4th accused is still a member of the Communist Party.
Despite the fact that he denies connection with the Communist
Party he has refused so far to state for what reason he was
in possession of the literature, upon which the prosecution
of the four persons in custody is being based.

Evidence For
There appears to be very little in
defence of Wong Ah Sz. He admits that
he obtained the literature found in his
room and that seized from the 1st and
2nd accused from a member of the
Communist Party but denies that he is a
member.

COMMENT
Enquiries made of the Chinese Authorities reveal that the 3rd accused Chien Zung and the
4th accused Wong Ah Sz are both agents of Han Lu Hao employed in the Public Safety Bureau and that he
is in direct contact with them. The 1st accused Wong Kiu Zeh Ts and the 2nd accused Koh Tuh Sai are
also alleged to be working for Han but make their report, etc. through the 3rd and 4th accused. All
the accused subsequent to their arrest made statements which despite the fact that they were corroborative
in general show points which are not consistent with fact. All have in one way or another stated that
they are agents of the Public Safety Bureau employed in the detection of communist activity but they
have failed to show the reason why they were jointly in possession of or concerned with the literature,

第四被告 王阿四，化名丁洪春

不利证据
1934年12月8日晚9点，第三被告钱成被警察逮捕时，就第一和第二被告被捕时身上持有的宣传品接受了讯问。他声称是从一名叫王阿四（化名丁洪春）的人那里获得的宣传品，此人住在乌拉尔路235号。警察突袭了该地址，并在那里逮捕了上述第四被告。对该男子居住的房间进行搜查后，发现了与从第一和第二被告处缴获的性质相似的共产党宣传品。王阿四受到严密讯问，他声称在他家中发现的宣传品以及1934年12月7日交给钱成以便在黄九子家中处理掉的宣传品，是从一名广东籍共产党员那里获得的。他在审讯中承认，这名广东人经常到他家拜访，但与他（王的）政治活动无关。他承认自己曾是共产党员，直到1934年1月向当地公安局自首。毫无疑问，第四被告王阿四仍然是共产党员。尽管他否认与共产党有联系，但他至今拒绝说明他持有作为起诉这四名在押人员依据的宣传品的原因。

有利证据
为王阿四辩护的理由似乎很少。他承认从他房间发现的宣传品以及从第一和第二被告处缴获的宣传品是从一名共产党员那里获得的，但否认自己是党员。

评论
向中国当局查询后得知，第三被告钱成和第四被告王阿四均为公安局雇员韩鲁浩的代理人，且韩与他们直接联系。据称，第一被告黄九子和第二被告高德山也为韩工作，但通过第三和第四被告提交报告等。所有被告在被捕后所作的陈述，尽管大体上相互印证，但显示出与事实不符之处。所有人都以某种方式声称他们是公安局受雇侦缉共产党活动的代理人，但他们未能说明为何共同持有或涉及因逮捕而被缴获的宣传品，

seized as the result of their arrest. Had they been in possession of a few handbills such as are obtained for information purposes the matter would not have looked too much like a conspiracy but the quantity actually found in their possession precludes the possibility that it was intended for intelligence purposes. Further none of the accused are prepared to state how long they have been in the employ of Han Lu Hao or whether they have brought about the arrest of communist on previous occasions.

Han Lu Hao alias Kuang Zeu Nyi as mentioned in Files D.5682 and 5711, appears to be given to irregular conduct in the matter of obtaining evidence against political offenders. Taking this circumstance into consideration there is every possibility that the four men in custody being employees of Han Lu Hao's, were in the act of planting evidence on some individual with the intention of later causing his arrest.

SECRET
ostensibly
Mr. Yeu Ding Ih, Nanking Political Agent in Shanghai, attended this office on the afternoon of December 14 when he stated in connection with this case that there was no intention on the part of the four accused to encompass the arrest of any person with the aid of the literature seized in their possession. He claimed that the literature had been obtained by the 4th accused for the purpose of passing on to the Public Safety Bureau. Relative to the large quantity of literature seized in connection with this case, Mr. Yeu stated that the 4th accused was in contact with the lower organs of the Communist Party and in posing as a member of the Communist Party had obtained the literature for distribution. In view of this it was necessary for the 4th accused to dispose of the whole lot. It was his efforts, stated Mr. Yeu, in forwarding the literature to his employer which caused the arrest of himself and the other three.

如果他们只持有少数用于获取情报目的的传单，此事看起来就不太像阴谋，但实际上在他们身上发现的数量排除了用于情报目的的可能性。此外，没有任何被告愿意说明他们受雇于韩鲁浩多久，或者以前是否曾促成过共产党的逮捕。

如档案D.5682和5711中所述，韩鲁浩（化名广泽义(音译)）在获取针对政治犯的证据方面似乎行为不端。考虑到这一情况，完全有可能这四名在押人员作为韩鲁浩的雇员，当时正试图栽赃陷害某人，意图随后导致其被捕。

机密
表面上
南京驻上海政治代理人叶定一（Yeu Ding Ih(音译)）先生于12月14日下午来到本办公室，他就此案表示，四名被告无意利用在他们身上缴获的宣传品来构陷任何人被捕。他声称，第四被告获取这些宣传品是为了移交给公安局。关于在此案中缴获的大量宣传品，叶先生表示，第四被告与共产党的下层组织有联系，并通过伪装成共产党员获取了用于分发的宣传品。鉴于此，第四被告有必要处理掉整批宣传品。叶先生称，正是他将宣传品转发给雇主的努力导致了他自己和其他三人的被捕。

My name is Wong Kiu Shih Ts, age 20, native

as a signal boy where I continued for three years.

The communistic literature in possession of
which I was arrested by police was handed over to me

being. My father discovered in my room the bundle

as it may be inflammatory literature. I called upon
Chien at his home but he was out, therefore I decided
to return the literature through Kao Tuh-sai who is a
friend of Chien Zung. When I handed over the bundle
with literature to Kao at Lai Yue Li Alleyway at

高德山（Kao Tuh-sai）
永州                                      D... Tchremshansky
南京路警察局    1934年12月8日                     Clerkish -e1-:

我叫高德山，23岁，永州人，码头苦力，住梧州路雷安里46号。我是文盲。我父亲曾是永州的码头苦力，在我年幼时去世。我13岁时来到上海，住在霞飞路（Rue Lafayette）姨妈家。当我16岁时，我在杨树浦的各个码头当码头苦力。大约两个月前，经钱成介绍，我认识了公安局特工韩鲁侯（韓魯侯），并从那时起开始作为他的线人工作。我被告知要监视码头上的共产主义活动并向他报告，但到目前为止我尚未做任何报告，因为我没有任何经验。
11月8日下午4点左右，我遇到了黄九子（黃九子），他告诉我钱成把一些文献留在了他家。他父亲建议他将文献归还给钱成。下午5时20分，我在梧州路雷悦里遇到黄九子，当他把文献交给我时，我被逮捕了。
我从黄九子那里接过文献，因为他请求我将其归还给他无法找到的钱成。

（签名）高德山。

Chien Zung (錢 成 )
Yangchow                                      D.S. Tchernshanaky
Kashing Rd Station    8/12/34                 Clerk Loh Wei-kong

My name is Chien Zung alias Ling Ming-sung
(林明生), age 21, native of Yangchow, residing at
143 Tsung Yang Li (春陽里) off Suchow Road. I am
a wharf coolie. My father was a wharf coolie at
Yangchow. I studied several months in my native place
at a private tutor when I was a child. I came to
Shanghai when I was 14 years of age. When I came to
Shanghai, I resided at my relative's home at Chapei.
At 17 years of age I became a wharf coolie at Japanese
wharf at Wayside, where I am working at present.
About two months ago I met one named Chiang ( )
who introduced me to Han Luhao (韓魯侯), agent
of the Political Section of Bureau of Public Safety.
He proposed me to work as his informer. I succeeded
in making acquaintance with a communist named Hsiao Zung
(小陽 ). This man told me to carry out communistic
work among the wharf coolies, and paid me $5.00 per month
in addition to the rent of my room, $6.00.

I am not a communist and was working only
on instructions of Han Lu-hao who also paid me $3.00
for my work as his informer. The communist literature
in my possession was obtained from Ting Hung-chun
(丁鴻君). I do not know where he received this
literature.

(Signed) Chien Zung

钱成（Chien Zung）
扬州                                      侦探员 Tchernshanaky
嘉兴路警察局    1934年12月8日                 职员 罗伟康

我叫钱成，别名林明生（Ling Ming-sung），21岁，扬州人，住苏州路春阳里143号。我是一名码头苦力。我父亲曾是扬州的码头苦力。小时候，我在家乡跟随私塾老师学习了几个月。我14岁时来到上海。来到上海后，我住在闸北亲戚家。17岁时，我在汇山路（Wayside）的日本码头当码头苦力，至今仍在那里工作。
大约两个月前，我遇到一个姓蒋（Chiang）的人（ ），他把我介绍给公安局政治科特工韩鲁侯（韓魯侯）。他提议我为他做线人。我成功结识了一位名叫小阳（Hsiao Zung）的共产党员。这个人让我在码头苦力中开展共产主义工作，除了支付我每月6美元的房租外，还每月付给我5美元。

我不是共产党员，只是按照韩鲁侯的指示工作，他也为我作为他的线人的工作支付我3美元。我持有的共产主义文献是从丁鸿君（Ting Hung-chun）那里获得的。我不知道他是从哪里得到这些文献的。

（签名）钱成

My name is Ting Hung-chun alias Wang Ah-tz
(王阿四), age 29, native of Nanking, wharf coolie,
residing at 200 □□ road. I am illiterate. My father
was a tailor. My parents died several years ago. I
came to Shanghai when I was seven years of age and
resided at my aunt's home at Suchow Road. Then I was
eleven years of age I became an apprentice at a glass
factory at Unpai. Three years later I became a wharf
coolie at Yangtsepoo where I am working until present.

In September 1933, I met one Kao Lao-sz
(高老四) who was also a wharf coolie, and through
his introduction I made acquaintance with one Cantonese
named Ho (吳), who was later arrested by the
Chinese Authorities for being a communist. I joined
the Communist Party through the introduction of Ho.
When I was a member of a Communist Party I received
from the Party $8 per month and the rent for my room,
$8.00.

In January 1934 I surrendered to the local
Bureau of Public Safety and since that time served
as an informer to an Inspector of the Political Section
of the Bureau in question. I made reports regarding
the activities of members of the Communist Party
and received $5.00 per month for this work. One month
ago I start to work under another agent of Bureau of
Public Safety named Han Lu-hao (韓魯侯). At the
same time I made acquaintance with one communist who

Communist Literature found in possession of
Kao Tuh Sai (高德山 ) at 5.20 8/12/34 in
Lai Yue Li Alleyway off Wuchow Road

1. 95 booklets entitled "Cartoons depicting Red Armies
to proceed to the North to Resist Japan", purporting
to emanate from the "Young Men's Truth Paper Office",
dated November 3, 1934.

2. Some 650 copies of four different kinds of coloured
leaflets entitled "A letter to the Youths and Masses
in Kiangsu in commemoration of the 7th Anniversary
of the Canton Uprisings/", purporting to emanate
from the "Kiangsu Provincial Executive Committee of
the China Communist Youth Group", dated December 11.

3. Some 250 copies of a pamphlet entitled "A letter to
the Youths over the efforts to crash the 5th Campaign
by the Imperialistic Kuomintang", purporting to
emanate from the "Shanghai Committee of the Communist
Youth Group", dated December 1, 1934.

4. Some 300 copies of a pamphlet entitled "Young Men's
Truth Paper", Issue No.72, dated November 20.
It contains articles opposing the attack of the
Soviet districts by the Kuomintang, and news relating
to the victories of the red army, as well as the
anti-Japanese activities of volunteers in the North
East. In addition, it relates the oppression of
the ricsha coolies by the Ricsha Board of the S.M.C.
